title: Run Qwen 3.8 Flash Next (125B) on consumer hardware (RTX 4090) at 100T/s
why_read: Running a large 125B-parameter model at high throughput on a single consumer GPU is a genuinely notable practical engineering feat worth understanding.
analysis: The post describes getting a sizeable language model running locally on an RTX 4090 at a reported 100 tokens per second, which would be unusually fast for a model of that scale on consumer hardware. This likely involves aggressive quantization, mixture-of-experts routing, or clever memory offloading tricks that are of real interest to people doing local LLM inference. The title names seem to reference models/numbers that may be exaggerated or satirical, so some skepticism about exact claims is warranted. Still, the underlying topic, squeezing large models onto affordable hardware, is a recurring and valuable engineering theme.
